metaDescription: Six corded pet hair vacuums compared on weight, dust cup size, brush roll design and filtration, with honest notes on wrapped hair and bare floor scatter.
expertTake: The Shark NV752 TruePet is the best overall pick because it combines a powered lift-away pod, a large dust cup and HEPA filtration. The Eureka Airspeed is the value pick for small homes and anyone who finds a big upright heavy. Skip a corded upright if you live mostly on stairs or in a multi-level home with no outlets nearby, because the cord becomes the main chore.
introParagraphs: Pet hair is a different cleaning problem from dust. It weaves into carpet, wraps around brush rolls and floats back up from hard floors, so the best pet hair vacuums are chosen for brush design, bin size and filtration rather than headline suction.

The six machines here are corded uprights and sticks, which keep full power for as long as you plug in. Differences come down to weight, how well each handles a brush roll full of hair and how easy it is to reach under furniture and up the stairs.

products.name: Shark NV752 Rotator TruePet upright with powered lift-away and HEPA
products.description:
The Shark NV752 TruePet is built around a powered lift-away design: the pod detaches and keeps a motorised brush running, so you can clean under furniture and across stairs without losing agitation. It has swivel steering, LED headlights and a large dust cup, which matters because pet hair fills a bin faster than dust does. A HEPA filter and sealed system target the fine dander that pets shed.

The tradeoff is weight and bulk. As a full upright with a pod, it is heavier than the Eureka Airspeed and takes more storage space. Compared with the Shark Rocket stick, it offers more bin volume and a deeper clean on carpet, but a stick is easier for quick floor passes.

In ownership terms, empty the dust cup after each use, snip any hair wrapped around the brush roll and wash the filters on the maker's schedule, letting them dry fully before reuse. The pod is the reason to choose this model for stairs and upholstery in a pet household.
products.bestFor: Multi-pet homes with carpet, stairs and upholstery that need a powered lift-away.
pros: Powered lift-away keeps a motorised brush going on stairs and furniture
Large dust cup suits the volume of pet hair
HEPA filtration and sealed system target dander
Swivel steering and LED headlights help around furniture
cons: Heavier and bulkier than lightweight uprights and sticks
Brush roll still needs hair snipped away regularly

products.name: Eureka Airspeed NEU10AE5 lightweight 7.7 lb pet hair upright
products.description:
The Eureka Airspeed is the lightest vacuum in this lineup at 7.7 lb, and it is aimed at buyers who find a full-size upright awkward. A quick-release handle lets you clean above the floor, and its compact shape stores in a small closet. It handles carpet and hard floor with one brush roll.

The tradeoff is capacity and features: it has a smaller dust cup than the PowerSpeed and no powered lift-away. Compared with the NV752, it is easier to lift up a flight of stairs but weaker for a multi-pet home. It is the lowest cost tier of the six, so expect a simpler build and a basic tool set.

In ownership terms, empty the cup after every session when pets shed heavily, because a full cup cuts suction. Snip hair off the brush roll every few weeks and wash the filter as the maker directs. It is a sensible pick for apartments and for older owners who need a light machine.

products.name: Eureka PowerSpeed NEU181A 10 lb upright with 2.6 liter dust cup

specList.label: Floors
specList.value: Pet hair, carpet and hard floor

products.description:
The Eureka PowerSpeed has a 2.6 liter dust cup, one of the larger bins in this lineup, and a 960 W motor. At 10 lb it sits between the featherweight Airspeed and the heavier Shark uprights. The big cup suits a home with a long-haired dog, because it means fewer trips to the bin.

The tradeoff is that wattage is not a measure of cleaning performance; suction at the nozzle depends on airflow, brush design and seal. Compared with the Airspeed, you gain about 2.3 lb and a larger cup. Compared with the NV752, you lose the powered lift-away, so stairs rely on the hose and tools.

In ownership terms, empty the cup outdoors if possible, since hair and dust cloud easily. Cut the hair from the brush roll, wash the filter, and let it dry for a full day before refitting. It is a good mid-weight choice for a medium home.

products.name: BISSELL CleanView Swivel Pet 2252 upright with scatter-free technology
products.description:
The BISSELL CleanView Swivel Pet pairs swivel steering with a triple-action brush roll and a scatter-free design intended to stop debris being flicked across hard floors. That is a real issue with pet hair, where a spinning roll can push loose fur away rather than pick it up. The pet-focused tool set helps with upholstery and stairs.

The tradeoff is that it lacks a powered lift-away and a HEPA pod, so allergy sufferers may prefer the Shark or the BISSELL Pet Hair Eraser. Compared with the Eureka PowerSpeed, it handles bare floors with less scatter but gives up some cup volume. Its weight is mid-range.

In ownership terms, clean the filter and brush roll regularly, and empty the bin when it is about two-thirds full. It suits homes that have a mix of rugs, hardwood and tile with a dog or cat.

products.name: BISSELL Pet Hair Eraser Allergen Lift-Off 39883 with HEPA sealed system
products.description:
The Pet Hair Eraser 39883 uses a lift-off detachable pod and a HEPA sealed allergen system, which makes it the most filtration-focused BISSELL in this lineup. The pod lets you carry the vacuum for stairs and car interiors, and the sealed system keeps fine dander in the machine rather than venting it. It is aimed at households where someone reacts to pet allergens.

The tradeoff is that a HEPA path restricts airflow, so filters need regular washing or replacement. Compared with the NV752, the pod is not motorised, so pod cleaning relies on tools rather than a spinning brush. It costs more than the CleanView and offers the strongest filtration among the BISSELLs.

In ownership terms, wash or replace the filters on the maker's schedule and let them dry fully before refitting. A clogged filter drops suction and raises noise. It is a good fit for allergy-prone households with a dog or cat.

Lift-off pod makes stairs and car interiors easier
Pet Hair Eraser tools target upholstery and stairs
Swivel steering and mixed-surface cleaning
cons: Pod is not motorised, unlike the Shark NV752
HEPA filter needs regular washing or replacement

products.name: Shark Rocket Pet Plus HV322 corded stick and handheld in one
products.description:
The Shark Rocket Pet Plus is a corded stick that converts to a handheld, so it handles floors, stairs and upholstery with one machine. Being corded, it keeps full power and never runs out of battery in the middle of a room. A lighter frame than an upright makes it easy to carry.

The tradeoff is bin size: a stick holds less hair than the NV752 or PowerSpeed, so heavy shedders need frequent emptying. Compared with the Eureka Airspeed, it is more versatile because it converts to a handheld, but it is a stick shape that is less stable. It also lacks the sealed HEPA design of the BISSELL 39883.

In ownership terms, empty the bin after each use, cut hair from the roll and wash the filter. It is good for small homes and light shedding. A multi-pet home with a lot of carpet needs more capacity.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Pet hair wraps around a brush roll and cuts agitation within weeks if you do not snip it. Self-cleaning or anti-tangle designs reduce wrapping but never eliminate it. The common mistake is believing a marketing claim of zero tangles. Plan on a monthly snip on any of these, and keep a small pair of scissors or a seam ripper in the vacuum closet. In a long-haired dog household the roll can need attention every two weeks, and the sign is a faint burning smell or a roll that spins slowly.

Pet hair is bulky, so a larger cup means fewer trips to the bin. The Eureka PowerSpeed lists 2.6 liters, and the Shark NV752 is described as large. Sticks such as the Rocket are smaller. A full cup reduces suction, so size matters more than people expect. Emptying at the two-thirds line keeps airflow healthy, and a wider cup mouth stops hair from bridging across the opening and hanging in the bin. A cup that you can empty with one hand over a bag is worth more than a few extra ounces of capacity.

Uprights run roughly 8 to 18 lb, and the weight is felt on stairs. The Airspeed at 7.7 lb is the lightest, and the PowerSpeed is 10 lb. Lift-away pods let you leave the body behind. Buyers often forget stairs until after purchase. A standard stair tread is roughly 10 to 11 in deep, so a wide upright head cannot sit on one; you will hold the body in one hand and the hose in the other, or lift the pod away. If you have a carpeted staircase and a cat, a lift-away or a stick that converts to a handheld will save your back.

A HEPA filter in a sealed system keeps fine dander in the machine instead of venting it into the room. It also restricts airflow, so washable filters need regular care. The BISSELL 39883 and Shark NV752 are the HEPA-sealed models here. Sealing only helps if the filters are clean and seated, so inspect the gaskets when you wash them. Dander also lives in carpet and fabric, so slow passes and several strokes per area matter as much as the filter in the machine.

A brush roll that is ideal on carpet can scatter fur across hard floors. Scatter-free designs and brush-off switches help. The BISSELL CleanView Swivel Pet is designed around that issue. Check whether the roll can be turned off. On a hardwood floor with a long-haired cat, a brush-off or soft-roller mode often picks up more than spinning bristles do. Also check the nozzle height: a head that sits too high will skim over low carpet and leave hair behind.

A corded vacuum offers steady power but is limited by cord length and outlet position. Count outlets on your route before buying. A lift-away or handheld mode extends reach without moving plugs. Most corded household vacuums have a cord in the range of 20 to 30 ft, and the lineup listings do not all state it, so measure the farthest corner from your outlet and add the distance you need for stairs before you commit.

maintenance.why: A full cup cuts suction. Pet hair compacts, so empty before it fills.
Wrapped hair reduces agitation. Cutting with scissors takes a minute and restores performance.
Clogged filters reduce suction. Dry them fully for 24 hours before refitting.
Pet hair blocks narrow passages. Clearing them restores airflow.
A frayed cord is a hazard. Wind it loosely to avoid kinks.

faq.q: Is an upright or a stick better for pet hair?
faq.a: Uprights hold more hair and clean carpet more deeply. Sticks are lighter and quicker for floors and stairs, but fill sooner.

faq.q: Do anti-tangle brush rolls really work?
faq.a: They reduce wrapping, but long hair still builds up over weeks. Plan to cut it away from time to time.

faq.q: Do I need HEPA for pet allergies?
faq.a: A sealed HEPA system helps keep fine dander inside the machine. It also needs regular filter care to keep airflow.

faq.q: Will a corded vacuum be enough for a big house?
faq.a: Yes if outlets are reachable, because power stays constant. A lift-away pod or handheld mode extends reach.

faq.q: Why does my vacuum scatter fur on hardwood?
faq.a: A fast brush roll can flick light hair away. Use a scatter-free design, a soft roller, or turn the brush off.

faq.q: How often should I replace filters?
faq.a: Follow the manual. Washable filters last longer if cleaned monthly and dried fully, but replace them when damaged.
